question: Will Spain win the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the national team that wins the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

If at any point it becomes impossible for this team to win the FIFA World Cup based on the rules of FIFA (e.g., they are eliminated in the knockout stage), this market will resolve immediately to “No”.

If the 2026 FIFA World Cup is permanently canceled or has not been completed by October 13, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from FIFA, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.excerpt: Spain defeated Portugal 1-0 in the round of 16, with Mikel Merino scoring a late winner assisted by Ferran Torres. Spain returned to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time in 16 years and would next face the United States or Belgium.

Spain defeated Portugal 0-1 at Dallas Stadium thanks to Merino's goal in the 91st minute. Following this victory, Spain would face the winner of USA–Belgium in the quarter-finals on Friday, July 10, at 9:00 pm CEST.

Luis de la Fuente said Nico Williams had completed training with the group but was returning from an injury and a short period of inactivity. Whether Williams received minutes against Portugal would depend on the development of the match.

Spain beat Austria 3-0 through two goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and one from Pedro Porro. It was Spain's first World Cup knockout victory since its title-winning run in 2010. Unai Simon's clean sheet was his fifth successive World Cup shutout, including the 2022 match against Morocco, and extended his run without conceding to 519 minutes.

Spain sealed first place in Group H and eliminated Uruguay with a 1-0 victory. Alex Baena scored Spain's goal, and Uruguay's Agustin Canobbio received a stoppage-time red card for a challenge on Pau Cubarsi.

Cape Verde held Spain to a 0-0 draw on its World Cup debut. Lamine Yamal came off the bench in the second half, while Ferran Torres hit the crossbar before halftime. Spain entered the tournament after winning Euro 2024 but had failed to advance beyond the round of 16 in each of the previous three World Cups.
